facts.statement: The type species Protospinax annectans was discovered in the Solnhofen limestones of southern Bavaria.
facts.quote: The type species, P. annectans, was found in the Solnhofen limestones of southern Bavaria.

facts.statement: Additional specimens of P. annectans were found at Harvard University in the 1990s after being previously misidentified as Squatina and Heterodontus.
facts.quote: Formerly known from only two specimens, further museum specimens of P. annectans were discovered at the Museum of Comparative Zoology of Harvard University in the 1990s, having been misidentified as Squatina and Heterodontus.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of P. annectans measured approximately 1.63 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was a relatively small shark, with the largest uncatalogued specimen of P. annectans measuring about 1.63 m long.

facts.statement: A 2023 study classified Protospinax as a squalomorph shark, though its exact position within the group remains tentative due to a lack of unambiguous traits.
facts.quote: A 2023 study found it to be a squalomorph shark; one analysis placed it closest to angelsharks and sawsharks, but the authors concluded that its exact position within Squalomorphi is ultimately tentative due to a lack of unambiguous supporting traits.

facts.statement: Protospinax was formerly classified in the order Squaliformes but was reclassified into its own order because that classification was paraphyletic.
facts.quote: Antiguamente se consideraba como parte del orden Squaliformes, pero debido a que esta clasificación era parafilética, fue reclasificado en su propio orden.

facts.statement: Protospinax is considered a clade more closely related to sawsharks (Pristiophoriformes) and angelsharks (Squatiniformes).
facts.quote: Convirtiéndose en un clado más cercano a los tiburones sierra (Pristiophoriformes) y tiburones ángel (Squatiniformes).

facts.statement: Protospinax is characterized by a skull articulation fitting between the maxilla and cranial box, and dorsal fins bordered by smooth spines.
facts.quote: Se caracterizaba por poseer un cráneo tiene una articulación que encaja entre el maxilar y la caja craneana, además que sus aletas dorsales estaban bordeadas por espinas lisas.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Protospinax was a benthopelagic shark that fed on various invertebrates with thin to hard shells, measuring between 1 and 1.6 meters.
facts.quote: Se sugiere que era un tiburón bentopelágico que se alimentaba de diversos invertebrados de caparazón delgado a duro, siendo relativamente pequeño debido a medir entre 1 a 1,6 metros.

facts.statement: Protospinax lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic in Europe and Russia.
facts.quote: Protospinax is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish from the Middle to Late Jurassic of Europe and Russia.

facts.statement: Protospinax existed from the Toarcian to the Maastrichtian, spanning 184.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Maastrichtian (184.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 2025, Begat and colleagues proposed moving three nominal species previously assigned to Protospinax into new genera.
facts.quote: In 2025, Begat and colleagues assigned three nominal species previously assigned to Protospinax to represent new genera.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the Early Jurassic record likely represents an indeterminate Protospinax species, and only the Valanginian record from France can be reliably assigned to the genus among Early Cretaceous records.
facts.quote: They also suggested that the Early Jurassic (Toarcian) record likely represents an indeterminate species of Protospinax, and that among the putative Early Cretaceous records, only the Valanginian record from France can be reliably referred to this genus.
